site.title: Stromfenster: when is electricity cheap and clean?
site.description: Stromfenster shows when electricity in Germany is cheap and clean, based on day-ahead prices and the generation mix.
site.question: When is electricity in Germany cheap and clean?
site.intro: Day-ahead prices and the expected share of wind and solar, for today and tomorrow.

states.unavailableTitle: The data is not available right now
states.unavailableText: The service that provides prices and generation data did not answer. Please try again in a few minutes.
states.stale: There is no price for the current quarter hour. The figures below may be out of date.

best.heading: When should I run it?
best.nonePrice: No window of {n} h is left in the prices published so far.
best.noneForecast: No window of {n} h is left in the forecasts published so far.
best.tomorrowNote: Tomorrow's prices are published in the early afternoon. Until then the cheapest window is within today.

priceNote.text: These are wholesale prices. A household pays them only with a dynamic tariff, and then with taxes, levies and grid fees on top.

price.title: Price
price.subtitle: Day-ahead wholesale price in ct/kWh, per quarter hour. Without taxes, levies and grid fees.

price.caption: Hourly mean in ct/kWh

share.title: Wind and solar

factors.caption: Direct CO₂ emissions in grams per kWh of electricity

notes.generation_other_conventional: Mineral oil, waste, gases from coal and steel production, and other fuels. The source has no value for this group; the hard coal value is used in its place.
notes.generation_pumped_storage: The electricity was generated, and counted, when the water was pumped up.
notes.generation_biomass: The source counts no CO₂ for renewable fuels.
notes.generation_other_renewables: The source counts no CO₂ for renewable fuels.
